Edge score and Wald statistics

Source: R/selection.R
mc_edge_scores.Rd

Computes, for every pair of responses, a chi-squared(1) statistic that ranks edges of the Gaussian graphical model (GGM) layer without refitting the whole model. The precision matrix is parametrized linearly, \(K_b = \sum_d \eta_d Z_d\), with one diagonal parameter per response and one parameter \(\eta_e\) per edge, so that an edge is absent exactly when \(\eta_e = 0\). Present edges are scored by the Wald statistic \(\hat\eta_e^2 / \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\eta_e)\), with the variance read from the model-based covariance \(J^{-1}\) stored in the fit. Absent edges are scored by the efficient Pearson score, that is, the score of the candidate coordinate after projecting out the nuisance parameters \(\lambda\) of the current model, $$u_e = \psi_e - J_{e\lambda} J_{\lambda\lambda}^{-1}\psi_\lambda, \qquad S_e = u_e^2 / \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(u_e),$$ where \(\psi\) is the second-order Pearson estimating function and \(J\) its sensitivity. With variability = "model" the variance is taken under the working identity \(V = J\) (second Bartlett identity), in which case it equals the Schur complement \(J_{e\cdot\lambda} = J_{ee} - J_{e\lambda}J_{\lambda\lambda}^{-1} J_{\lambda e}\); with variability = "empirical" it uses the empirical fourth-moment variability of the Pearson contributions, which is the appropriate choice when the second Bartlett identity fails.

Usage

mc_edge_scores(
  fit,
  which = c("both", "wald", "score"),
  variability = c("model", "empirical")
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph" (GGM layer).

which

one of "both" (default), "wald" (present edges only) or "score" (absent edges only).

variability

"model" (default, working \(V = J\)) or "empirical" (fourth-moment variability) for the absent-edge scores. It does not affect the Wald statistics of present edges.

Value

A data frame with one row per pair of responses (restricted by which) and columns i, j (response indices with \(i<j\)), present (logical, edge in the support of the fit), stat (Wald statistic for present edges, efficient score for absent ones), p_value (chi-squared(1) upper tail of stat), stat_unadjusted (unadjusted score \(\psi_e^2/J_{ee}\), only for absent edges, NA otherwise) and variance (estimated variance of \(\hat\eta_e\) for present edges, of \(u_e\) for absent ones). The attribute "variability" records the choice used. An edge whose estimated variance is not finite and positive has stat and p_value equal to NA, and mc_graph_stepwise does not take a present edge in that state as a removal candidate.

Details

Dividing \(\psi_e^2\) by the unadjusted \(J_{ee}\) ignores the estimation of the remaining parameters and, because \(J_{e\cdot\lambda}\le J_{ee}\), understates the statistic. That quantity is returned as stat_unadjusted, for ranking, but it does not carry a chi-squared calibration.

The reported p_value is a working reference distribution: it is the chi-squared(1) tail of stat. Its validity requires the regularity conditions of the second-order estimating functions and, for variability = "model", the working identity \(V = J\). Applied to edges chosen by a search over graphs, it remains descriptive.

The function refuses fits whose numerical diagnostics explicitly mark graph-layer inference as uncertified. Responses are indexed \(i<j\) over all \(R(R-1)/2\) pairs.

See also

mc_graph_stepwise, which uses these statistics to rank candidate edges.

Other structure selection: mc_graph_penalized(), mc_graph_stability(), mc_graph_stepwise(), mc_select_lambda()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 200; x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = rnorm(n), y2 = rnorm(n), y3 = rnorm(n), x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_edge_scores(f)
#>   i j present        stat   p_value stat_unadjusted    variance
#> 1 1 2    TRUE 0.125702663 0.7229300              NA 0.005119502
#> 2 1 3    TRUE 0.006452406 0.9359773              NA 0.005113397
#> 3 2 3    TRUE 0.323259426 0.5696554              NA 0.005129649
# }
